title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors (and the CEO)
tiers.description: Directors of any AGT Group Company, including the CEO for procedural purposes; approval route is the Chairman and the Board via the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees of any AGT Group Company other than the CEO; approval route is the CEO (or Company Secretary if the CEO is absent or involved in the Dealing).

windows.start_anchor: day following release of the AGT Half-yearly and Preliminary Final results and Dividend Announcements
day following the Annual General Meeting
commencement of the offer or application period specified in a prospectus or supplementary prospectus for a new share issue
windows.end_anchor: close of that offer or application period

rules.detail: Securities is defined as shares, options, preference shares, debentures and convertible notes issued by AGT Group Companies (plus certain other companies' securities); it does not extend to third-party financial products referencing AGT's share price. A physically-settled OTC collar creating an agreement to deliver AGT shares could fall within 'enter into any agreement or arrangement' to Deal, but a cash-settled derivative is not addressed.
No concept of hedging or limiting economic risk appears anywhere in the Policy.

Not named. An agreement with a bank to sell or deliver AGT shares (e.g. a prepaid forward) is an 'agreement or arrangement' to deal in a security, so it is a Dealing requiring Board approval (Directors/CEO) or CEO approval (Employees) and must occur within a Window Period or under an exceptional-circumstances approval.
rules.evidence: 'Deal' means to subscribe, purchase, sell, assign, transfer, encumber or otherwise alienate any right, title or interest in a security, or to enter into any agreement or arrangement to do so.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named; only a general ban on trading 'for a short term or speculative gain' exists, which is captured under short_term.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

A cash-settled CFD referencing AGT's share price transfers no right, title or interest in a Security and is not an agreement to deal in one, so it falls outside the 'Deal'/'Securities' definitions as drafted.

Not named as a distinct topic, but the Policy contemplates margin lending: entering a margin loan encumbers the shares (a Dealing requiring approval within a Window Period or exceptional-circumstances consent), while a secured lender's forced sale on default is expressly excluded from the Policy altogether.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Encumbering a security is expressly named as a form of Dealing, so granting a charge, lien or pledge over AGT shares requires Board approval (Directors/CEO) or CEO approval (Employees) and must occur within a Window Period or under an exceptional-circumstances approval.
rules.evidence: 'Deal' means to subscribe, purchase, sell, assign, transfer, encumber or otherwise alienate any right, title or interest in a security, or to enter into any agreement or arrangement to do so.

rules.detail: Any financing arrangement that encumbers AGT shares (not limited to margin loans) is a Dealing under the express 'encumber' limb, requiring approval and window-period timing; there is no outright prohibition.
rules.evidence: 'Deal' means to subscribe, purchase, sell, assign, transfer, encumber or otherwise alienate any right, title or interest in a security

rules.detail: General ban on trading for short-term or speculative gain, with no stated holding period or basis.
rules.evidence: will not trade in Securities for a short term or speculative gain

clearance.evidence: For any proposed dealing or during a Window Period, a Director and the CEO may Deal in Securities subject to notifying and obtaining the prior approval of the Board.

clearance.approver: CEO (or Company Secretary if the CEO is absent or involved in the Dealing)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 3 days of the Dealing being transacted
clearance.evidence: During a Window Period an Employee (other than the CEO) may Deal in Securities subject to notifying and obtaining the prior approval of the CEO (in the absence of the Company Secretary or if the Dealing involves the Company Secretary).

whether the Director or Employee is bound by a court order, enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement to transfer or sell their Securities
a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the final date for the exercise ... falls outside a Window Period and the restricted person could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at a time when free to do so.

where a Director or Employee is a trustee, trading in the Securities by that trust, provided that the Director or Employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade outside a Window Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

exemption_authority: The Company Secretary (or CEO) may grant written approval to Deal outside a Window Period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order/enforceable undertaking, or other exceptional circumstances where the dealing is the only reasonable course), and the dealing must complete within 14 days of approval or any earlier period specified. Confidentiality of a grant or refusal is not addressed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities to which this Policy applies include ... all ordinary shares (including shares subscribed for), share options, preference shares, debentures, convertible notes or any other form of security issued by any of the AGT Group Companies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-issued OTC put or call over AGT shares is not itself a 'Security' issued by an AGT Group Company, so a cash-settled collar leg may sit outside the Policy entirely; only the encumbrance of the underlying shares (loan security) and any agreement to deliver them are clearly caught as Dealings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: 'Deal' means to subscribe, purchase, sell, assign, transfer, encumber or otherwise alienate any right, title or interest in a security, or to enter into any agreement or arrangement to do so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting security over the collared shares for the bank loan requires Board approval (for Directors/CEO) or CEO approval (for Employees) and must be timed within a Window Period or approved as an exceptional circumstance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy does not apply, and Dealings in Securities can be effected by Directors and Employees outside Window Periods, in the following circumstances: ... a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the Policy, so it is not blocked by Window Periods or the approval procedure even if it occurs at a closed time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Cover letter dated 15 December 2010 lodging the Board-adopted Securities Trading Policy with the ASX.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a 2010-era policy with no derivatives, hedging or margin-lending-specific regime; confirm with the company whether a more recent policy has since superseded it before relying on this analysis.

summary: A funded collar is workable in outline but rests on a narrow and dated policy. The 'Deal' definition expressly includes encumbering a security, so granting the bank security over the collared shares requires Board approval (for Directors/the CEO, via the Company Secretary) or CEO approval (for other Employees), timed within a Window Period (30 days after half-year/full-year results or the AGM, or a prospectus offer period) or approved as an exceptional circumstance, with post-trade notice to the Company Secretary within 3 days. The Securities definition is limited to instruments issued by AGT Group Companies, so a cash-settled OTC put and call written by a bank may not constitute 'Securities' or a 'Dealing' at all under this Policy's terms, leaving the derivative legs largely unregulated except to the extent they involve an agreement to deliver shares. Critically, a secured lender's forced sale on default (e.g. under a margin lending arrangement) is expressly excluded from the Policy and can occur even outside a Window Period, which favours the bank's enforcement position. No provision addresses vesting status, minimum shareholding, or financing disclosure, so those risks are unaddressed and should be confirmed directly with the company, including whether this 2010 policy remains current.
